name: emu-dm-desync
description: Reproduces the stale one-sided DM-session bug (issue this rig exists to catch) and exercises the #138 self-heal, DETERMINISTICALLY. A DMs B ('DM ALPHA') and the session establishes (asserted: ALPHA renders on B). At a fixed instant B drops its own session half in-process (EMU_DROP_DM_SESSION_AT_MS) while staying up and still neighboring A, so A keeps its stale session; A's next DMs ('DM BETA', scheduled to begin AFTER the drop) land on a B with no session, so B logs 'Failed session decrypt' (the desync symptom) and then 'DM session desync ... re-initiating handshake (self-heal)' (the #138 receiver-side heal). run_scenarios.sh asserts the ALPHA screen render plus both log signatures. The construction is event-driven end to end: the sender's 'neighbor' destination waits for discovery (no silent broadcast fallback), and the drop waits for the session to exist before tearing it down, so tick-loss skew on CI pods (subjective firmware time running slower than wall time, at different rates per code path) cannot fire either step early. duration_ms is a wall-clock cap with skew headroom, not a schedule. Every run reaches the constructed state: the drop replaces the old reboot, whose RAM-clear/beacon-reacquisition/stale-DM-window races made the symptom probabilistic. Neighbor discovery is made reliable with a short emulator beacon interval (EMU_BEACON_INTERVAL_MS) so the ALPHA DM never falls back to a broadcast. The full heal-and-redeliver still completes (A tears down its stale session on B's re-INIT and a later BETA decrypts); that end-to-end redelivery keeps some real-time variance, so CI gates on the deterministic symptom+heal-trigger rather than the final BETA render.
